extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on attacker-controlled data — Remote code execution on the server — pickle can execute arbitrary Python during deserialization [verified: Same pickle.loads() deserialization as idx 2: attacker-controlled bytes from request.body or GET 'blob' enable arbitrary code execution.]

Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads() in ops endpoint case_bundle_thaw_181 — Attacker with the ops token can achieve remote code execution on the server by sending a crafted pickle payload, leading to full system compromise. [verified: pickle.loads() on attacker-controlled data from request.body or GET 'blob' parameter allows arbitrary code execution; no input validation or safe deserialization intercepts the input.]

Arbitrary code execution via eval() in ops endpoint case_formula_cast_264 — Attacker with the ops token can achieve arbitrary Python code execution on the server, leading to full system compromise, data exfiltration, or lateral movement. [verified: eval() on attacker-controlled 'expr' GET parameter with restricted builtins is bypassable via class introspection; token gate does not neutralize arbitrary code execution.]

Code execution via eval on attacker-controlled expression — Remote code execution — arbitrary Python evaluation via bypass of restricted eval globals [verified: Same eval() code injection as idx 1: bypassable restricted eval on attacker-controlled 'expr' GET parameter enables arbitrary Python execution.]

Hardcoded default Django SECRET_KEY — Attacker can forge Django session cookies, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens, leading to complete authentication bypass and account takeover for all users. [verified: SECRET_KEY on line 10 uses 'insecure-local-dev-key-change-me' as a hardcoded fallback when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset. No .env file exists in the repo and load_dotenv silently skips it, so the default known key is used, enabling session/CSRF/password-reset token forgery.]

security finding — Session forgery and CSRF token bypass if the application deploys without setting the env var. [verified: Duplicate of finding 0: the same hardcoded 'insecure-local-dev-key-change-me' SECRET_KEY fallback at line 10 is reachable because no .env overrides it, enabling cryptographic forgery of sessions and tokens.]

DEBUG=True by default with hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY and insecure cookie flags in debug mode — Session forgery, CSRF token bypass, password reset token forgery via known SECRET_KEY; debug error pages leak stack traces, SQL, and settings; media files served without auth; cookies lack Secure flag [verified: Combined effect of default SECRET_KEY='insecure-local-dev-key-change-me', default DEBUG=True, Secure cookie flags omitted (gated on not DEBUG), and media served without auth via static() in DEBUG mode: all these insecure defaults are live because no .env file exists to override them.]

Reflected XSS via ops endpoint case_caption_fold_076 — Attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of anyone viewing the response, leading to session hijacking, credential theft, or DOM manipulation. [verified: GET parameter 'copyline' is concatenated directly into HTML with no escaping; the token gate is access control, not output sanitization, and does not neutralize the reflected XSS.]

Path traversal — arbitrary file write via unvalidated 'name' GET parameter — Arbitrary file write outside the intended private_exports directory, enabling code execution or system compromise [verified: Same path traversal as idx 3 and 12: unvalidated 'name' GET parameter enables arbitrary file write via BASE_EXPORT_DIR concatenation.]

XXE via lxml parser with resolve_entities and load_dtd enabled on attacker-supplied XML — Arbitrary local file read, SSRF, and denial of service via XML external entity expansion [verified: Same XXE as idx 4: lxml parser with resolve_entities and load_dtd enabled on attacker-controlled XML body allows file reads and SSRF.]

security finding — Arbitrary file write on the server, potentially leading to code execution (e.g. overwriting Python modules or cron jobs). [verified: Same path traversal as idx 3: unvalidated 'name' GET parameter concatenated to BASE_EXPORT_DIR enables arbitrary file write outside intended directory.]

NoSQL injection via attacker-controlled MongoDB query in ops endpoint case_mongo_lane_608 — Attacker with the ops token can execute arbitrary JavaScript on the MongoDB server via $where operator, bypass query filters, extract all data, or cause denial of service. [verified: Entire request.body JSON is passed as MongoDB find_one() query with no field allowlist or operator sanitization, enabling $where JS execution and query manipulation.]

XML External Entity (XXE) injection in ops endpoint case_xml_fold_619 — Attacker with the ops token can read local files (e.g., /etc/passwd, .env secrets), perform SSRF to internal services, or cause denial of service via billion laughs attack. [verified: lxml parser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False parses attacker-controlled request.body XML, enabling XXE file reads and SSRF.]

security finding — Detailed error pages expose stack traces, settings, and environment variables to unauthenticated attackers. Media files (including privileged legal documents) are served without access control. [verified: Duplicate of finding 1: DEBUG defaults to True when DJANGO_DEBUG is not set, exposing sensitive debug information and serving media files without authentication through the static() path gated on DEBUG in urls.py line 64.]

security finding — Non-admin users (attorneys) can bypass matter status transition rules, e.g. skipping the mandatory CLOSED state before archiving or jumping from INTAKE directly to ARCHIVED. [verified: matter_update (line 337-347) calls form.save() on MatterForm which includes 'status' in Meta.fields with no clean_status() or clean() override to validate transitions. The parallel matter_status_update view properly uses Matter.transition_to() and ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS, but matter_update bypasses it entirely, letting an attorney POST status=archived directly from any state.]

CSV formula injection in matter, deadline, and document exports — When a staff member exports and opens a CSV in a spreadsheet application, attacker-crafted data (e.g., a matter titled =cmd|'/C calc'!A0) can execute arbitrary commands or exfiltrate data from the spreadsheet user's machine. [verified: The _csv_response function (line 750-756) writes CharField values directly via csv.writer with no prefixing/sanitization of formula characters (=, +, -, @). No form validation, model clean(), or middleware prevents formula-triggering characters in matter titles, client names, document titles, or tags. Staff-role users can inject arbitrary data into these fields.]

CSV formula injection — exported CSVs contain unsanitized string fields that can execute spreadsheet formulas — Formula execution in spreadsheet software when exported CSVs are opened, enabling command execution or data exfiltration [verified: Same unsanitized _csv_response path as finding [0]; export_matters (lines 772-773) writes item.title and item.client.name — both unrestricted CharFields — directly through csv.writer with no formula-character prefixing. No compensating control exists anywhere in the form, model, or view layer.]

Sensitive data exposure in logs — request body and Authorization header logged at WARNING level — Leakage of potentially sensitive tokens/headers into application logs; log injection for log-forgery attacks [verified: Same log injection and credential exposure as idx 7 and 14: raw body and Authorization header logged without sanitization.]

Log injection and credential exposure in ops endpoint case_wire_tally_224 — Attacker can inject forged log entries to mislead investigations or cover tracks, and any Authorization header (bearer tokens, basic auth) sent to this endpoint is written to application logs where it may be accessed by unauthorized personnel or leaked in log dumps. [verified: logger.warning logs raw request body (enabling newline-based log injection) and Authorization header value (exposing bearer tokens/credentials in plaintext logs); no sanitization or redaction is applied.]

security finding — Secrets, API keys, or bearer tokens sent to this endpoint are permanently recorded in application logs. [verified: Same log injection and credential exposure as idx 7: raw body and Authorization header logged at WARNING without sanitization or redaction.]

Weak PRNG — random.choice used for nonce generation with user-controlled length in ops endpoint case_nonce_roll_599 — Predictable nonce values enabling attackers to forecast future tokens and bypass any security controls relying on nonce unpredictability. [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) is not cryptographically secure for nonce generation (CWE-338); the user-controlled 'length' GET parameter (line 153) enables trivially short, predictable nonces with no compensating CSPRNG fallback.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification in ops endpoint case_trust_drift_648 — Network attackers can intercept and modify traffic to the partner endpoint, potentially injecting malicious responses or exfiltrating data sent in the request. [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables TLS verification on a reachable code path; the hardcoded dummy URL does not neutralize the dangerous pattern.]

security finding — Session cookies may be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, enabling man-in-the-middle session hijacking. [verified: No SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS is set anywhere in settings.py, and SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT defaults to False. With cookie Secure flags also gated on not DEBUG, sessions can be transmitted over plain HTTP, enabling MITM session hijacking.]

Missing rate limiting on login endpoint enables credential brute force — Attacker can brute-force user credentials without throttling, lockout, or CAPTCHA, leading to account takeover and access to client PII, privileged legal documents, and confidential matter data. [verified: Identical absence of rate limiting confirmed: no lockout, CAPTCHA, or throttle mechanism in settings.py MIDDLEWARE, INSTALLED_APPS, or requirements.txt; the LoginView at line 13 uses bare as_view() with no decorator wrapping. Reachable login path with unlimited attempts enables credential brute-force against all user accounts.]

Information disclosure via exception details in ops endpoint case_pulse_spill_351 — Attacker discovers internal filesystem paths (private_exports directory location), aiding in further path traversal or file-based attacks. [verified: RuntimeError message exposes BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path in JSON response; the token gate does not prevent path disclosure to any token holder.]

Information disclosure — environment variable and filesystem paths exposed in JSON response — Disclosure of internal deployment paths and Django settings module, aiding further targeted attacks [verified: Same information disclosure as idx 9 and 13: DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and BASE_EXPORT_DIR paths exposed in JSON response.]

Weak authorization — plaintext badge value 'lead' grants elevated lane in ops endpoint case_badge_gate_628 — Privilege escalation via trivially guessable authorization token, granting elevated lane access to any caller who sets the badge to 'lead'. [verified: Badge authorization compares cookie/header value against guessable plaintext 'lead' with no cryptographic protection, but the endpoint is already behind INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN gate and the 'elevated' lane response confers no access to additional resources or endpoints.]

security finding — Exposure of internal environment variable values and server filesystem paths, aiding further attacks. [verified: Same information disclosure as idx 8-9: case_trace_panel_638 and case_pulse_spill_351 expose internal paths and env vars to token holders.]
